sections.heading: Function
sections.text: This is a fictional procedure written for a synthetic test corpus. It does not describe any real facility. The interlock protects cooled equipment from loss of flow. FLOW_LOW_WARN is raised below 32 L/min. FLOW_LOW_LOW is raised below 25 L/min, and the cooling permit is removed 0.2 seconds later. Loss of the cooling permit removes the downstream permit.

sections.heading: Reading the event
sections.text: A real low-flow event shows the measured flow falling for several seconds before the trip, usually with the control valve opening to compensate and loop pressure falling. If measured flow was normal when the permit was removed, the trip may be false; see PL-TS-031.

sections.heading: Response
sections.text: Find the cause of the flow loss: pump trip, closed valve, leak or blocked strainer. Restore flow above 35 L/min and hold for 60 seconds before requesting a reset under PL-OP-032.

sections.heading: Escalation
sections.text: Escalate to the controls lead after 2 low-flow trips in one shift.

sections.heading: Response
sections.text: Restore flow above 30 L/min before requesting a reset.

documents.title: PL-TS-031 Diagnosing stale signals, chatter and communication loss

sections.heading: Stale signal
sections.text: This is a fictional procedure written for a synthetic test corpus. It does not describe any real facility. An analog reading that repeats exactly the same value for more than 10 seconds is stale. Real readings always show small noise. A stale signal does not trip anything by itself but hides a real change. Check the transmitter and the input card.

sections.heading: Chattering input
sections.text: A discrete input that changes state more than 4 times within 2 seconds is chattering. Typical causes are a loose terminal or a switch at the edge of its setpoint. If a permit was removed by a chattering input while the related analog measurement was normal, treat the trip as suspected false and inspect the wiring before any reset.

sections.heading: Communication loss
sections.text: If every analog reading from one rack goes missing at the same moment and returns at the same moment, the cause is the remote I/O link, not the process. Check the COMM_LINK events. Do not interpret missing data as zero.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.text: State in the summary which of the three patterns was found and what evidence supports it.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.text: This is a fictional procedure written for a synthetic test corpus. It does not describe any real facility. A permit may be reset only after the cause of the trip is identified and removed. A permit must never be bypassed or forced.

sections.heading: Steps
sections.text: Confirm the initiating alarm has cleared. Have a second person verify the readings independently. Press reset once. If the permit does not latch, stop and escalate.

sections.heading: Suspected false trips
sections.text: A suspected false trip still requires the cause to be found. Resetting to see whether it happens again is not permitted.
